overall: The AG found the Rowley Finance Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law on the three in-scope allegations (speaking limits, minutes, and budget copy) and declined to review the non-OML claims.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged he was denied the ability to fully participate at the March 12 meeting when the Chair stopped him from continuing to speak about a tree.
allegations.key_passage: Because public participation is at the chair’s discretion, the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting by limiting the Complainant’s ability to speak at the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Chair wrongly denied his request to have his comments on the tree safety risk included in the March 12 minutes.
allegations.key_passage: meets the Committee’s obligation under the Law to create and maintain accurate meeting minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee violated the law by not providing a copy of an FY20 Tentative Budget document when he requested it at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: because the Open Meeting Law does not require a public body to provide copies of documents to meeting attendees, we find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it did not provide the budget documents.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged age discrimination; the letter declined review because it falls outside the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: We do not address these allegations as they fall outside of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged profanity was used toward him; the letter declined review because it falls outside the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: We do not address these allegations as they fall outside of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee violated G.L. c. 87, § 3; the letter declined review because it falls outside the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: We do not address these allegations as they fall outside of the Open Meeting Law.
